title: HoldToConfirm
description: Button that runs its action only after being held down, for destructive actions whose consequence is already visible.

c.v: A button that runs its action only after the person holds it down for a set time. A fill advances across the button while it is held and rewinds when released early. Use it for destructive or hard-to-undo actions, like deleting a branch or force pushing, where the consequence is already visible on screen.

items.v: It is a native button. Its accessible name is the visible text (the confirmed label once done). The duplicate copy of the label used for the color flip is
points to a visually hidden hint that explains the hold time and the keyboard use. The hint and the live status are siblings of the button, so they do not become part of its name.
Mouse, pen and touch use pointer events with capture. Sliding more than 24px outside the button cancels the hold. A pointer cancel (for example the browser taking a vertical scroll) cancels it too.
Holding Space or Enter fills the button. Releasing early or tabbing away (blur) cancels. Key repeat is ignored.
Releasing early rewinds the fill on a spring that starts from rest. A quick re-press resumes from the current position.
